video_title: GTA 6, Money, Gangs, Crime, Prison & Biggest Jewelry Thief in US History | Lex Fridman Podcast #505
transcript: - The following is a conversation with Larry Lawton, one of the most notorious and prolific jewelry thieves in US history, who was eventually caught by the FBI, spent more than a decade in prison, including a lot of time in the hole, and then he turned his life around to run the Reality Check program that helps keep at-risk youth out of prison. He now hosts a YouTube channel where he breaks down real crimes, prison life, and how realistic the heists in movies and video games are with, of course, a lot of focus on Grand Theft Auto 3, 4, 5, and now GTA 6. This conversation is in two parts. The first part we recorded just now focused on GTA 6 and some other recent topics. The second part we recorded a while back, and it tells the timeless story of his life, the heists, the mob, the prison time, and what it takes to rebuild a life after losing everything. In this conversation and in general, Larry holds nothing back: sex, violence, drugs, robberies, all of it. He is also, in the time I've known him, a truly kind human being, which to me is a humbling glimpse into the complexity of human nature and the paths each of us can take in life and the evolution each of us can go through in life. This is the Lex Fridman Podcast. To support it, please check out our sponsors in the description where you can also find links to contact me, ask questions, give feedback, and so on. And now, dear friends, here's Larry Lawton. All right. For people who don't know, you were one of the most prolific, notorious jewelry thieves in US history. You were arrested by the FBI, served your time in prison, and since then you've done a lot of good for the community helping at-risk youth. And we'll talk about your life, we'll talk about your history, we'll talk about the whole journey in prison, but first we've gotta talk about GTA 6. - I'm an open book, Lex, you know that. And I'm glad to be here. You know, I think you do great work, and I think this is gonna be great- ... because you played the game. - Yeah, I played in terms of Grand Theft Auto, I played GTA 1, GTA 2, 3, Vice City, 4, and 5. The world that they created is bigger than life. A lot of the things that we love about movies, a lot of the things we love about video games. And I think in terms of GTA 6, in terms of places that are bigger than life, I mean, Miami, South Florida, this is your stomping ground. Like, how does that feel that Grand Theft Auto 6, likely the biggest game of all time by far, is set in this place where you operated as a jewelry thief? - It's... I'm going crazy. When I found out, what happened was I- - You're basically a GTA 6 character, Larry. - Yeah. I mean, it's kinda crazy that way because I didn't know what GTA was really. I heard of it like everybody else. But I got into it, and it's really amazing. I got into it so much, I'd lose my head in this game. And then I kept thinking what I would do in this game, what I would do. And that's what made me start really thinking more about GTA and the game and the crimes, 'cause that's what I did. My headquarters was down there in Mia... I started that... Well, my first robbery was in South Florida. It was a setup. But the, the game, I'm dying to see how they really portray an actual robbery, the actual how much they use for the casing. I've cased stores for two weeks, and I've cased stores for six weeks. You know, I mean, it could take forever to case a store. And I knew everything about a store. And if they wanna do a robbery right, they have to do it from when is the mailman coming, when is packages delivering, when is the sun setting, sun rising, so you could see the glare in the windows. There's so many variables that go into a robbery. And, you know, being I did so many, probably 25 or more, and, you know, I robbed so many that I had to travel up the East Coast to keep robbing. And I couldn't rob in New York because of affiliations with organized crime. They're protected. You know, you don't just go into a store in New York and rob it, especially my day in the '90s, '80s and '90s, because what happened then, it's protected by the mob. They get protection.
